answer: Persistent Queue Position: an identity must occupy a live processing slot for N consecutive epochs before its votes count. Slots are scarce and expire on idle, so an attacker cannot forge standing without paying real queue-time across every puppet. Each extra identity must harbor a separate slot, and holding many slots means paying sustained attention costs in parallel — the attacker's throughput collapses. Honest agents keep one slot warm; a Sybil fleet resembles an island of idle waiters losing their place.
